hints.title: Unbounded Reuse Without Duplicate Permutations
hints.text: The same number may be chosen an unlimited number of times to reach a target sum. How can you explore repeated choices without generating duplicate permutations like [2, 3] and [3, 2]?

hints.title: Forward Index Restriction Invariant
hints.text: Restricting candidate choices to the current index and forward prevents permutations of the same combination from being generated again.

hints.title: Target Pruning Backtracking Procedure
hints.text: Define a recursive search function with the remaining target, current combination path, and start index. If remaining target is 0, add a copy of path to results and return. If remaining target is negative, return. Otherwise, iterate through candidates from start index to end: append candidate, recurse with remaining target minus candidate keeping the same start index i, and pop to backtrack.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Branching tree has max depth T/M and branching factor up to N.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying all combinations without index ordering generates duplicate permutations of identical combinations, requiring expensive post-filtering.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting candidates enables early pruning when candidate > remaining target, reducing explored branches with O(T/M) stack space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Pruning when remaining < 0, passing index i (not i + 1) to allow reuse while preventing duplicate permutations, clean backtracking undo step.
